title: Adaptive-runtime send-composition correctness execution
purpose: Satisfy REQ-QUIC-CRT-0223 through REQ-QUIC-CRT-0228 by independently reviewing the two approved actuation candidates, promoting only exact passed proofs, authorizing one deny-by-default correctness-only two-axis cell, executing it through existing batch and buffer mechanism seams, rebuilding the immutable evidence chain, and independently reviewing the result.
design_summary: Original candidate bundles stay immutable. An additive review-result contract records independently recomputed content and promotes only the two exact axis/value pairs into the v2 family catalog. A versioned authorization document binds a correctness_only interaction plan, validation, compiled manifest, exact reviewed proof hashes, catalog and constraint versions, and one two-axis cell. Runtime plumbing receives only a compact immutable fixed-field snapshot, rejects ordinary or mismatched configuration, and retains the existing one-axis path. A bounded focused harness invokes the production batch selector, buffer policy, runtime evidence sink, owner token, and release seam. Offline tooling materializes and projects the resulting immutable evidence, then a separate reviewer recomputes all authority and evidence before issuing its result.
data_and_state_considerations: The runtime does not load JSON catalogs or proof documents. The compact authorization snapshot is internal and correctness-only; it contains exact fixed enum values and content identities, with both active and performance authorization false. Evidence remains bounded and composite-keyed. Candidate, review, authorization, proof, and review-result documents are immutable canonical JSON. The fifteen projection inputs remain the analytical authority chain, supplemented by exact authorization and review references.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The historical candidate binary path may be overwritten, so promotion requires a freshly generated proof whose exact committed source and binary identity are verifiable.
The batch proof must derive selected count from the production selector rather than prefill an expected result.
The buffer proof must use the production policy decision's applied source count rather than a caller-provided expected count.

A single_eligible batch actuation supplies one selected write, so buffer distinctness cannot occur on that same operation; both axes may nevertheless actuate on separate attributable opportunities in one exact authorized cell.
Candidate, missing, stale, wrong-value, or revoked proof metadata denies authorization.
Any third behavior-distinct axis, outside-family axis, active authorization, performance authorization, or manifest mismatch denies before mechanism execution.
Every rented combined owner requires exactly one terminal release with complete composite identity.
Shadow recommendations never affect the applied mechanism, and rollback clears both fixed-field forced values.
alternatives_considered: Mutate candidate documents in place to passed. Rejected because it destroys the original review input.
Load family and proof catalogs on the runtime hot path. Rejected because catalog authority belongs to offline tooling.
Remove the one-axis guard generally. Rejected because only one exact reviewed correctness cell is authorized.
Change batch or buffer mechanisms to force same-operation dual actuation. Rejected because mechanism semantics and lower-only safety authority must remain unchanged.
Use expected fixture values as operation truth. Rejected because mechanism evidence must originate from production selectors and evidence seams.
risks: The correctness harness proves mechanism semantics, not network performance or measurement readiness.
The both-distinct result is cell-level across separate operations because the established supplies-work relationship makes same-operation dual actuation structurally impossible.
Additive plan and manifest authorization fields must preserve all retained v1 fixtures and regressions.
Repository-wide SpecTrace validation retains unrelated pre-existing failures.
open_questions: After this correctness milestone, which external review gate will govern any future measurement release?
Will later interaction families require a generalized signed authorization carrier, or is the fixed internal correctness token sufficient for their separately reviewed slices?
